EN: Open the Maneuver tool from the app bar for any craft in flight. You’ll need a level 3 Tracking station when playing career.
Select the part of the current crafts orbital plan that you want to create a maneuver in and choose your time format here.
The maneuver tool gives assistance plotting transfer and intercept maneuvers.
Useful information on the control you’re mousing over will appear here.
The mode control shows important information regarding the inputs and control of your vessel. It can be \nchanged between staging, docking and map modes.

Shows specialized control input 
indicators for the two docking 
modes: rotation (ROT) and 
translation (LIN).
Shows the active stage number \nand the stage lock indicator \n(green for go, purple for locked).
Note that the PYR Indicators \nchange to blue when precision \nmode is enabled.
Shows the state of the three \ninput axes and any trim applied.

This helps you understand your vessel's orientation. Think of it as a three-dimensional compass: the 
blue half of the sphere indicating away from the body you're orbiting (sometimes known as the sky 
when you are landed), the brown half is towards it (ground) and the line between them an artificial 
horizon.

To fix a part, EVA an engineer with repair kits in their inventory.  Get close to the damaged part, open its action menu, and click Repair.
Repair kits are consumed to effect the repair. Larger parts will need the supplies from multiple repair kits to repair them.
Some parts can get damaged due to challenges posed by space travel.
Kerbals can fix many of those broken parts by using a repair kit.
During flight you can monitor the fear - I mean excitement - of your astronauts via the portraits in the bottom-\nright corner. Hovering over a specific kerbal will give you detailed info on them.

Also known as Intravehicular 
Activity. Changes the camera 
to show you this kerbal's point 
of view.
The kerbal's name. Their role and \nskill level will be shown when the \ncursor is over a portrait.
Reveal the vessel's interior spaces. It's like \nlooking at the man behind the curtain.
*EVA while flying in atmosphere can be detrimental to a kerbal's health.
Extravehicular Activity: this \nkerbal will exit the spacecraft.*
Adjust how many portaits \nare shown in the list.

The staging stack helps you to visualize the vessel's current and upcoming stages. In flight mode It \nshows you how much fuel is attached to running engines, and also lets you adjust the stages "on the fly."
Remove Empty Stage:\nDeletes the stage next to the icon.\nNote: this only works for empty stages.
